source.title: New Reliquarian Nodes are SO MUCH BETTER Than Last League! | PoE 3.29 Build Shells
source.usage: Community shell ideas and risk framing. Treat as opinion until patch notes, PoB data, and in-game node behavior confirm it.

global_constraints.claim: Reliquarian does not simply award normal ascendancy points in the same way as regular lab progression.
global_constraints.coach_action: Avoid presenting first/second/third/fourth lab order as guaranteed until the final Reliquarian UI and point rules are confirmed.

global_constraints.claim: Node choices are path and point constrained, so build shells should not freely combine top, bottom, left, and right clusters.
global_constraints.coach_action: Recommend one primary shell path, then list optional defensive cross-path tests only when point cost is explicit.

global_constraints.claim: The top cluster should not be treated as directly reachable from the center. Current image reading indicates the build must route through the 9 o'clock or 3 o'clock side first.
global_constraints.coach_action: For Arakaali, Black Cane, Xirgil, Shimmeron, Sands of Time, or Femurs shells, require an explicit left-entry or right-entry path before recommending the top cluster.

global_constraints.claim: Combining a left defensive shell such as Dawnbreaker with a top offensive shell such as Arakaali is a cross-path plan, not a default combined shell.
global_constraints.coach_action: Do not recommend Dawnbreaker plus Arakaali as the core plan unless the final tree confirms enough points and pathing efficiency.

global_constraints.claim: Reliquarian-granted triggered skills such as Molten Burst and Raise Spiders may not behave like socketed item skills for support gem scaling.
global_constraints.coach_action: Mark support scaling as verify_in_pob_or_game before using it as main DPS.

entry_path.cross_path_warning: If paired with top cluster Arakaali or Black Cane, this becomes a left-to-top cross-path plan and must be point-checked.

shells.summary: Converts large portions of cold, lightning, and physical damage taken into fire damage, making one high maximum fire resistance plan extremely attractive.
enablers_to_test: Purity of Fire maximum resistance scaling
Watcher's Eye or other final 5 percent conversion sources if needed
risks: May compete with Melding defensive shell instead of stacking cleanly with it.
Requires careful fire resistance and maximum fire resistance planning.
Does not solve damage by itself.

shells.summary: Spell suppression, ailment avoidance, and life recovered on suppressed spell hits can carry builds that normally struggle to access suppression.
good_for: Templar or Marauder shells lacking suppression
risks: Only works against suppressed spell hits.
Needs remaining suppression and ailment avoidance solved through gear/tree.

entry_path.cross_path_warning: This is a left-entry life-stacking shell. Do not assume it also reaches top Arakaali or Black Cane without point-checking the left-to-top route.

shells.summary: Converts Energy Shield from equipped armour items into maximum Life, but pays a large level-scaling life penalty and removes Energy Shield as a defensive pool.
candidate_skills: Rathpith Globe plus Crown of Eyes attack conversion shells
Dark Pact or Relic-style life scaling if patch data supports them
enablers_to_test: high Energy Shield body armour, helmet, gloves, boots, and possibly shield if the final wording includes shields
Rathpith Globe if using maximum Life to scale spell damage or spell critical strike chance
Crown of Eyes only if converting spell damage into attack damage
Dissolution of the Flesh or other life-loss mitigation only if the final build supports that playstyle
strong life recovery, recoup, leech, or regen
breakpoints: At level 90, the node's -12 Life per level penalty is -1080 maximum Life.
At level 100, the node's -12 Life per level penalty is -1200 maximum Life.
The shell only becomes attractive if Energy Shield gained from equipped armour items exceeds that penalty by enough to justify losing Energy Shield.
risks: High ES armour pieces can create suffix and attribute pressure while the build still needs resistances and recovery.
Removing all Energy Shield makes hybrid ES recovery, Ghost Dance, and normal ES buffer plans unavailable.
If the damage engine does not scale from maximum Life, this may be only an expensive defense shell.
Rathpith-style versions must handle life sacrifice or life reservation mechanics during T16 mapping.

entry_path.pathing_note: Do not assume this can be opened directly from the center; choose a 9 o'clock or 3 o'clock route first.

shells.summary: Triggered Raise Spiders can be used as a poison damage and attack speed engine for attack builds if spider uptime is solved.
enablers_to_test: The Writhing Jar-style worm flask for boss spider startup
Dark Monarch-style spider count scaling if available
risks: Requires kills or spawned worms to create spiders on bosses.
Has ramp-up time.
Ascendancy-triggered Raise Spiders support scaling must be verified.

entry_path.pathing_note: Do not assume this can be opened directly from the center; choose a 9 o'clock or 3 o'clock route first.

shells.summary: Phantasmal Might adds flat physical damage to spells per summoned phantasm, pushing physical spell hit builds rather than pure minions.
enablers_to_test: Dark Monarch-style phantasm count scaling if available
risks: Phantasm uptime and count are the real build gate.
May lose too much by giving up a rare weapon and shield.
Needs patch notes to confirm spell buffs or final skill choices.

entry_path.pathing_note: Top cluster path must be paid through a side route first.

shells.summary: Block-triggered energy shield recharge can become a major recovery layer with max block and Wicked Ward-style recharge protection.
risks: Best on top-side block/ES trees.
Damage skill is still undecided.

entry_path.cross_path_warning: If paired with top cluster Arakaali or Black Cane, this is the right-entry route into top and must be point-checked.

shells.summary: Extra chain and non-chaos as extra chaos reward projectile builds that naturally chain.
risks: Good mapper shell, but single target and defenses must be solved.
Deadeye remains the natural baseline for many bow/projectile versions.

shells.summary: Melding without the normal large all-resistance penalty is a strong tank shell, especially if one maximum elemental resistance can be pushed high.
risks: Usually choose this as an alternative defensive plan to Dawnbreaker full fire conversion, not an automatic stack.
Requires one high maximum resistance plan.

entry_path.cross_path_warning: Treat this as a separate bottom route unless the final tree proves efficient access to side or top clusters.

shells.summary: Best viewed as a shock and Herald support package for attack builds, not as proof that pure Herald of Thunder autobomber is solved.
enablers_to_test: full physical-to-elemental conversion if the skill has physical damage
Herald of Thunder reservation with supports
separate HoT autobomber startup and spread package if using HoT as main damage
risks: Deal no Physical Damage is a real build constraint.
100% reservation efficiency halves reservation; it does not make Herald of Thunder free.
Do not assume Hits always Shock overrides Herald of Thunder's own shock restriction without in-game verification.

shells.summary: Melee hits can trigger Level 20 Molten Burst and gain fire penetration, but the trigger may be supplemental if support gem scaling is unavailable.
risks: Reliquarian-granted Molten Burst likely cannot be socket-supported like the axe version.
Cooldown and projectile scaling must be checked.
May not justify the whole path by itself.

shells.summary: Explosions require enemies taunted by warcries, so this is not a walking autobomber engine by default.
enablers_to_test: warcry automation or comfortable manual warcry rhythm
poison scaling from chaos explosion damage
boss add or worm setup if trying boss explosions
risks: Warcry requirement breaks simple autobomber feel.
Explosion condition and boss usefulness are narrow.
Do not confuse this with Obliteration-style kill explosions.

shells.summary: Physical damage builds can gain large extra elemental damage if Ruby, Sapphire, and Topaz flask uptime is solved.
risks: Requires three elemental flask slots or equivalent uptime.
Competes with other bottom path attack nodes.
Physical base damage must be high enough.

shells.summary: Reducing maximum frenzy charges to zero can keep the no-frenzy critical multiplier condition always active.
risks: Jewel socket opportunity cost.
Only a damage stat shell, not a complete build.

autobomber_relevance.hot_autobomber_verdict: Fidelitas' Spike keeps Herald of Thunder interesting, but the video transcript supports treating it as an attack/herald shock shell first. A pure HoT autobomber still needs independent startup, shock spread, Storm Secret self-damage sustain, and boss single-target validation.
autobomber_relevance.warcry_explode_verdict: Al Dhih is not a core autobomber engine because it is warcry-gated and warcry taunt is mandatory.

t16_average_mapping_lens.purpose: Evaluate Reliquarian shells by average T16 mapping behavior, not by isolated node text.
t16_average_mapping_lens.baseline_assumption: Average T16 means alched rare maps with normal rare monster pressure, map boss present, common dangerous map mods filtered, and no expensive final gear unless explicitly listed.

evaluation_metrics.question: Does the build keep killing while moving, or does it stop frequently to set up?
evaluation_metrics.t16_fail_signal: Clear depends on manual setup every pack or loses uptime against tanky rares.

evaluation_metrics.question: Can the build kill T16 rares and map bosses without the mapping engine falling off?
evaluation_metrics.t16_fail_signal: Map clear is fast but rares or bosses require a separate unsupported skill that is too weak.

evaluation_metrics.question: Does the defensive shell handle many small hits, degens, ailments, and occasional large hits?
evaluation_metrics.t16_fail_signal: The build looks good in PoB but dies when recovery, suppression, ailment immunity, or max resistance is incomplete.

evaluation_metrics.question: How many common T16 map mods must be avoided?
evaluation_metrics.t16_fail_signal: The build bricks on reflect, less recovery, no regen, reduced aura effect, or ailment avoidance without clear regex rules.

evaluation_metrics.question: Are the required uniques and rares realistic before the build is expected to farm T16?
evaluation_metrics.t16_fail_signal: The shell requires multiple contested uniques or rare suffix pressure before it can safely enter red maps.

evaluation_metrics.question: How much button timing is required during normal T16 mapping?
evaluation_metrics.t16_fail_signal: The build only works if the player keeps multiple temporary buffs, warcries, flask states, or spawn setups perfectly aligned.

shell_specific_t16_gates.passive_tree_gate: Needs maximum fire resistance and fire resistance planning; otherwise conversion alone is not enough.
shell_specific_t16_gates.item_gate: Actual Dawnbreaker, Tempered by War, Purity of Fire, or equivalent conversion/max-res layers change the result heavily.
shell_specific_t16_gates.t16_note: Strong defensive base for T16, but it does not supply damage or clear speed.

shell_specific_t16_gates.passive_tree_gate: Needs enough maximum Life scaling and recovery to make the ES-to-Life conversion worthwhile after the -12 Life per level penalty.
shell_specific_t16_gates.item_gate: Requires high Energy Shield armour items and usually a life-scaling payoff such as Rathpith Globe or a life-as-resource damage engine.
shell_specific_t16_gates.t16_note: Promising if the build converts a large ES gear budget into both EHP and damage; weak if it is only a larger life pool with no damage payoff.

shell_specific_t16_gates.passive_tree_gate: Needs poison scaling, attack speed, wither or chaos amplification, and enough life/defense because the top path itself is not a full defense plan.
shell_specific_t16_gates.item_gate: Pneumatic Dagger and boss spider startup tools are build-defining; without them T16 bosses and tanky rares can stall.
shell_specific_t16_gates.t16_note: Promising if spider uptime and poison attack scaling are solved; weak if the build cannot create spiders during single target.

shell_specific_t16_gates.passive_tree_gate: Needs physical spell scaling, cast speed, conversion or added-as-extra scaling, and a defense package compatible with the chosen entry path.
shell_specific_t16_gates.item_gate: Phantasm count and uptime are mandatory; without them Black Cane is only a partial damage idea.
shell_specific_t16_gates.t16_note: Can become a real T16 spell shell only if phantasms stay up during rares and bosses.

shell_specific_t16_gates.passive_tree_gate: Needs conversion if using physical attacks, shock effect, and a separate single-target plan if Herald of Thunder is treated as damage.
shell_specific_t16_gates.item_gate: Pure HoT autobomber versions depend on Storm Secret, shock spread, recovery, and resistance pressure.
shell_specific_t16_gates.t16_note: Treat as attack shock/herald support first; do not assume it clears average T16 as a self-contained HoT autobomber.

shell_specific_t16_gates.passive_tree_gate: Needs warcry support, taunt coverage, and probably poison or explosion scaling.
shell_specific_t16_gates.item_gate: Automation or comfortable manual warcry rhythm changes the mapping feel more than the node text suggests.
shell_specific_t16_gates.t16_note: High operation load; not a default T16 walking autobomber.

shell_specific_t16_gates.passive_tree_gate: Needs one maximum elemental resistance pushed high and enough resistance budget to make the cap meaningful.
shell_specific_t16_gates.item_gate: Strongly depends on max-res sources and suffix pressure.
shell_specific_t16_gates.t16_note: Excellent defensive idea only after the item/tree package exists.

t16_average_mapping_lens.coach_rule: Before recommending a Reliquarian shell for average T16, state which passive tree gates and item gates are assumed. If those gates are missing, recommend a bridge build or fallback instead of the final shell.

mod_readiness_lens.answer: Raw game mods and an item-level candidate affix resolver exist, but Reliquarian shell-specific T16 required-affix scoring is still partial.

available_data_sources.limitation: Answers whether a mod can spawn on an item base; does not by itself decide whether that mod is good for a Reliquarian shell.
Large raw table; requires item tag/domain resolution before it can answer base-specific affix questions.
Good for rare defense bases, but not enough to decide Dawnbreaker/Melding/Storm Secret shell completion.
Not enough for Pneumatic Dagger poison attack, Black Cane spell, or Herald scaling decisions.
Needs shell-aware suffix pressure checks for resistance, attributes, chaos resistance, reservation, and unique ring/amulet slots.

available_data_sources.limitation: Useful for search text, but not yet mapped to each Reliquarian shell's required affix checklist.

mod_readiness_lens.coach_rule: If asked whether item-specific mod lookup exists, answer yes for spawnable prefix/suffix candidates via GGPKIndex.get_item_mod_candidates. If asked whether Reliquarian shell mod scoring is complete, answer no unless shell-specific rare affix groups have been mapped to concrete mod ids or trade stat ids.

coach_rules: When the user asks for a Scion Reliquarian build, compare shells before locking HoT.
Do not present Fidelitas' Spike as proof that Herald of Thunder can self-sustain shock or single-target.
Do not recommend Al Dhih for walking autobomber play unless the user accepts warcry-gated explosions.
For Guardian maps and Delve/Fossil goals, score Dawnbreaker or Melding defensive shells before offensive novelty.
For top cluster builds, test Arakaali poison attack and Black Cane physical spell shells as serious candidates, not side notes.
Never say the top cluster is directly reachable from the center; require a 9 o'clock or 3 o'clock entry path first.
For average T16 recommendations, evaluate passive tree gates, item gates, map mod tolerance, single-target patch, and operation load before ranking a shell.
Do not claim Reliquarian shell mod support is complete until shell-specific affix groups are mapped to concrete mod ids or trade stat ids.
